title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: protect files sent over FTP and SFTP
summary: The briefing passes: its controls, opt-in default, licensing and rollout statements are supported. One minor correction remains: cite Microsoft's offline-device documentation for the statement about devices awaiting an updated policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP can monitor and protect sensitive files transferred over FTP and SFTP.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) in Microsoft Purview can monitor and protect sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP from managed Windows devices.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: FTP and SFTP protection is admin-opt-in: it is not enabled by default and administrators must configure the transfer activities in Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: FTP and SFTP protection is not enabled by default. Administrators must configure FTP/SFTP transfer activities in Endpoint DLP policies to apply protection.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page describes protection from managed Windows devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) in Microsoft Purview can monitor and protect sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP from managed Windows devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP evaluates FTP and SFTP transfers against policy rules as it does copying to USB devices or network shares.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP evaluates these transfers against your policy rules, just as it does other device activities such as copying to USB devices or network shares.

claims.claim: FTP and SFTP transfer events can be reviewed in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: You can review the resulting events in Activity explorer.

claims.claim: The FTP and SFTP action is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Locations > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > File activities for all apps > Apply restrictions to specific activity > FTP and SFTP transfers.
claims.quote:
Under Actions, select Audit or restrict activities on devices.
5. In File activities for all apps, select Apply restrictions to specific activity.
6. Select the FTP and SFTP transfers checkbox, and then choose an action.

claims.claim: The FTP and SFTP transfer action supports Audit only, Block, Block with override and Allow.
claims.quote: Supported actions are Audit only, Block, Block with override, and Allow.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: FTP and SFTP rules support conditions such as sensitive information types or sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Create a rule, and add the conditions you want to detect, such as sensitive information types or sensitivity labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: FTP and SFTP transfers support full file evidence collection that can save a complete copy of a matched file.
claims.quote: FTP and SFTP transfers support full file evidence (FFE) collection. Enable evidence collection in Endpoint DLP settings and configure it in your DLP policy. When a user attempts to transfer a matched file, a complete copy can be saved.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes the feature as closing a gap in protection across common transfer methods.
claims.quote: It prevents unauthorized data exfiltration while maintaining visibility and control and closes a gap in protection across common transfer methods.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends starting with a small pilot group.
claims.quote: We recommend starting with a small pilot group and setting the action to Audit only.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Audit only before broad deployment and blocking.
claims.quote: Start with audit only mode before enabling blocking actions.

claims.quote: Example of an end-user notification for a blocked FTP transfer:

claims.claim: Activity explorer is not a real-time view.
claims.quote: Activity explorer isn't a real-time view.

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports up to 30 days of data.
claims.quote: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days worth of data.

claims.claim: Devices report endpoint activities only while online.
claims.quote: Devices report endpoint activities only while they're online. An offline device backfills its activities after it reconnects.

claims.claim: A device that has not received a new or updated policy is not covered by that policy version.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online. However, the outdated policy that exists on the offline device will still be enforced.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about#endpoint-dlp-and-offline-devices to sources for the statement about coverage before a device receives the latest policy.

claims.claim: Customer-managed evidence storage adds Azure storage charges.
claims.quote: Storage costs are charged in addition to the cost of your Entra subscription.

claims.claim: Microsoft-managed evidence storage is currently included in E5.
claims.quote: Storage cost today is included in E5.

claims.claim: Microsoft says it may charge additionally for excessive Microsoft-managed evidence storage usage.
claims.quote: However, Microsoft will monitor storage usage and may charge additionally based on excessive usage. This will be communicated to customers separately should there be a change in the business model.

claims.claim: Learn tells admins configuring customer-managed Azure evidence storage to consider access tiers and storage pricing.
claims.quote: Consider configuring Azure storage account access tiers and Azure storage account pricing.

claims.claim: Evidence collection lets administrators choose customer-managed or Microsoft-managed storage.
claims.quote: Select a storage type (Customer managed store or Microsoft managed store) and then select + Add storage.

claims.claim: The evidence collection settings provide a view of Microsoft-managed storage usage.
claims.quote: Click on View Usage button, a panel will open. Here you can see month wise graph of daily usage and also export the usage data.

claims.claim: On the Locations page, administrators can scope the device policy to selected users or device groups.
claims.quote: On the Locations page, select Devices, and then scope the policy to the users or device groups you want.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal path to Activity explorer is Data loss prevention > Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Activity explorer.

claims.claim: Export-ActivityExplorerData -StartTime <DateTime> -EndTime <DateTime> -OutputFormat Json exports Activity explorer events for a date range.
claims.quote: Export-ActivityExplorerData -StartTime "07/08/2022 07:15 AM" -EndTime "07/08/2022 11:08 AM" -OutputFormat Json

claims.claim: Export-ActivityExplorerData is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The event export reads events rather than changing policy.
claims.quote: Use the Export-ActivityExplorerData cmdlet to export activities from Data classification > Activity Explorer in the Microsoft 365 Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: The Export-ActivityExplorerData reference lists no FTP or SFTP activity filter value.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Export-ActivityExplorerData FTP SFTP activity filter'; opened learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/export-activityexplorerdata and read its complete valid activity filter list. No FTP or SFTP value is listed.

claims.claim: Evidence collection settings are in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Setup evidence collection for file activities on devices.
claims.quote:
Choose Data Loss Prevention.
3. Select Endpoint DLP settings.
4. Expand Setup evidence collection for file activities on devices and set the toggle to On.

claims.claim: The rule must select Collect original file as evidence for all selected file activities on Endpoint.
claims.quote: In Incident reports, select Collect original file as evidence for all selected file activities on Endpoint.

claims.claim: The evidence configuration must also select the FTP and SFTP transfers activity.
claims.quote: - FTP and SFTP transfers

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for configuring this FTP/SFTP evidence collection control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP evidence collection Set-PolicyConfig PowerShell EvidenceCollection storage'; opened evidence setup, Set-PolicyConfig and New-/Set-DlpComplianceRule references, searching evidence and FTP/SFTP. No documented setting operation found.

claims.claim: Per-device configuration and policy sync status are reached at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

DeviceInfo

| project DlpInfo

claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Defender portal

3. Query the DeviceInfo table
4. Expand the DlpInfo column to view Endpoint DLP device details

claims.claim: Devices must be online to receive policy updates.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen.
